solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: With little room in tents pitched around river

parts.note: to be in tents that have been pitched is to have camped

explanation.surface: Campers complain that their riverside tents leave them little space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In tents pitched' reads as the setting for the cramped feeling, but it is the verb CAMPED, which then wraps around the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Cramped means having little room, and 'with little room' works as the same adjectival phrase.

clue.text: Good conclusion to bad action film

indicators.note: a bad ACTION is one gone wrong, its letters knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A reviewer says a lousy action movie at least had a decent ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Action film' looks like a single phrase, but 'film' is the definition on its own; 'Good conclusion' is not the last letter of good but G placed at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a thin layer spread over a surface, as of dust or oil, is called a film.

clue.text: Score from ace cricketer getting runs in defeat

parts.note: A = ace, as on playing cards
R = runs on a cricket scorecard

explanation.surface: A star cricketer's runs contribute to the team's total even though they lose.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface makes 'Score' look like a run total; it is a golf score. A bat is crossword shorthand for a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an albatross is a score of three under par on a hole.

clue.text: Lost — died in foreign land

parts.note: Peru is a land foreign to the British solver

explanation.surface: A traveller went missing and died abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign land' is vague on purpose: any country could fit, and only the definition and crossings pin it to Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdu, borrowed from French, means lost or hidden from sight.

clue.text: Shy girl, doubly feminine, one needs to impress

parts.note: to dent is to press a mark into, to impress

explanation.surface: A timid, very feminine girl feels she has to make an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To impress' sounds like winning someone over; here it is the physical sense, pressing a mark into something.
explanation.definitionFit: Diffident means lacking confidence, shy.

clue.text: Ganesh as traitor to an extent in Hindu writings

indicators.note: the answer is found in the words only to an extent, spanning part of them

explanation.surface: Hindu scriptures partly portray the god Ganesh as a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Ganesh, the elephant-headed god, makes the Hindu setting feel like the point, which disguises that he is only a letter carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A shastra is a Hindu sacred treatise; the plural 'writings' is loose for a single work.

clue.text: Eddy initially showing desire

indicators.note: only the initial letter of 'showing' is taken

explanation.surface: A man called Eddy starts to show his feelings for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Eddy looks like a man's name at the head of the clue; it is the swirl of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge and an eddy are both movements of water, a rush or swirl.

clue.text: Museum loan has me crippled

indicators.note: the crippled letters no longer stand in working order

explanation.surface: A curator complains that lending out an exhibit has left them hamstrung.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashmolean is the university museum in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this is Oxford University's museum of art and archaeology, founded on Elias Ashmole's collection.

clue.text: Time wasted in member's area

parts.note: wasted and high both mean intoxicated

explanation.surface: Hours are wasted in the members' area of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' reads as time squandered, but it is slang for stoned. 'Member' is a limb, not a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Member' is a limb, and this is the upper part of the leg, a region of that member.

clue.text: Embarrassed because pressman eats meat

explanation.surface: A journalist is embarrassed about being seen eating meat.
explanation.walkthrough: A pressman in crosswords is usually ED, the editor; 'because pressman' together makes the shell that the meat goes into.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashamed and embarrassed both describe feeling awkward or abashed.

clue.text: Cautionary signal: right time to leave dance company

explanation.surface: A warning sign that it is the right moment to quit a dance troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: Rambert is a long-established British contemporary dance company; take away its first letter R and last letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is the traffic light that warns drivers to prepare to stop.

clue.text: Defence intelligence placed within hours on the spot

explanation.surface: Military intelligence is deployed within hours to the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defence intelligence' reads as one agency; it splits into a fort and wit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean at once, without delay.

clue.text: Disturbing to confuse sin with virtue

indicators.note: confusing the letters mixes them up

explanation.surface: It is troubling to mistake vice for goodness.
explanation.walkthrough: The moral surface keeps sin and virtue as opposites, when they are simply pooled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intrusive disturbs, as an intrusive noise does.

clue.text: Old characters making comeback exit play without permit

indicators.note: the exit comes back, running the other way

explanation.surface: Old actors return to the stage, walking out of a play they had no licence for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' suggests actors, reinforced by 'play' and 'exit', but they are letters of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogham is an ancient alphabet used for early Irish inscriptions, so its letters are old characters.

clue.text: Grand accommodation for new union member

explanation.surface: Smart lodgings are laid on for a new trade union recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union; the union here is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A groom has just joined a marriage, a new member of that union.

clue.text: Hired soldier showing forbearance about near-disaster?

indicators.note: a near-disaster makes a wreck of NEAR's letters

explanation.surface: A soldier for hire shows restraint when things almost go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near-disaster' is one hyphenated word on the surface, yet it splits into the fodder and its anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a professional soldier who fights for pay rather than for a country.

clue.text: Communicated with paper boy

parts.note: the Express, a British national newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone got in touch with the paperboy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper boy' reads as the lad who delivers newspapers; it splits into the Daily Express and Ed.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressed means put into words, communicated.

clue.text: Music, not French, stirred English blood

explanation.surface: A piece of music that was not French stirred English passions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not French' reads as an exclusion, but it is an instruction to translate 'not' into French, PAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A paso doble is a Spanish march-style dance, and also the music played for it.

clue.text: Naval base provides cover in South Africa on run

indicators.note: the cover goes in South Africa's abbreviation

explanation.surface: A naval base shelters ships while South Africa is under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Scapa Flow, in Orkney, was the Royal Navy's main wartime anchorage.
explanation.definitionFit: Scapa Flow served as a major British naval base in both world wars.

clue.text: Leaving ceremony is routine, girl admits

explanation.surface: A girl concedes that a farewell ceremony is mere routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving ceremony' suggests a school leavers' do; the leaving is from life.
explanation.definitionFit: The last rites are the sacraments given to someone about to die, a ceremony for one leaving this life.

clue.text: Nonsense writer without the polish

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside

parts.note: Edward Lear, writer of nonsense verse

explanation.surface: A writer of nonsense lacks refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking, but it is the old sense of outside. 'The polish' tempts as the definition, yet 'the' is needed for letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To leather something is to polish it with a leather cloth, such as a chamois.

clue.text: Elegantly simple opener from Hitchin Town

indicators.note: the opener of Hitchin is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tidy, stylish opening goal for Hitchin Town football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitchin Town is a real football club, which makes 'Town' look like part of its name; it is the definition on its own. Hitchin is in Hertfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: an industrial town in south Wales, near Swansea.

clue.text: Man had to suppress desire to be married

indicators.note: HE'D holds the desire down inside it

explanation.surface: A man had to rein in his urges to get married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man had' becomes the contraction HE'D, with the apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom: to get spliced or tied up in marriage, from harnessing two together.

clue.text: Saw woman for example headed west

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means running right to left

explanation.surface: Someone saw a woman, for instance, heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for an old saying. ADA reads the same either way, so only EG visibly turns.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Saw' is an old noun for a proverb or wise saying, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Iron block in Roman villa

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Iron blocks used in building a Roman villa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron block' could read as a building material for the villa, but it is the smith's tool, sitting across the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the iron block a smith hammers metal on.

clue.text: Robin left-wing as Bert's revolutionary?

indicators.note: a revolutionary AS BERT turns its letters over

explanation.surface: A man named Robin is as left-wing as his revolutionary friend Bert.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin reads as a man's name alongside Bert; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A folk name for the bird, from its orange-red chest.

clue.text: Reckoned explicit kiss should be cut

indicators.note: the kiss is cut out of the word

parts.note: explicit films once got the X certificate

explanation.surface: A censor judged that an explicit kissing scene should be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: X-rated was the old British film certificate for adults-only material.
explanation.definitionFit: Rated and reckoned both mean judged or estimated.

clue.text: Hydrophobic sailor with freehold?

parts.note: the 'free' half: to free is to rid; the 'hold' half tells it to hold the sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor who fears water happens to own property outright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freehold' is one word on the surface but splits into 'free' and 'hold'. Hydrophobia, fear of water, is a symptom of rabies.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrophobic can mean suffering from rabies, since hydrophobia is its classic symptom.

clue.text: Attempt to murder Caesar?

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second definition as playful: Caesar was stabbed to death, so to murder him is literally to have a stab.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is the idiom for making a try; the second is literal, since Caesar was stabbed to death.

clue.text: Forcibly expel ringer leaving one large church

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer is thrown out, departing a big church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringer leaving one large church' reads as a campanologist walking out; 'one large' is a single L, and BELL has two.
explanation.definitionFit: To belch is to forcibly expel smoke or gas, as a chimney belches smoke.

clue.text: Genuine assistance for auditor is passed on

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the words are taken as heard

explanation.surface: Real help for an accountant checking the books gets handed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like the accountant; in its root sense it is a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a message handed along from one person to the next.

clue.text: Given income? At finish was in debt!

parts.note: at the finish is at the end

explanation.surface: Someone was given an income yet still ended up owing money.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation splits the clue in two, hiding that the second sentence is pure wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a college or charity provided with a permanent fund has been given an income.
